THESE MFA'S HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, UMESH M ADIGA J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 4  JUDGEMENT Mr.Khansab vs Smt.Ashalata on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84050292/
3 Both these appeals arise out of the judgment and award dated 18.08.2016 passed in MVC No.2642/2014 by the V Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT-VI, Belagavi.

2. Respondent No.1 filed MFA No.103826/2016 challenging the liability fastened on him to pay the compensation and the petitioners-claimants have filed MFA No.103883/2016 praying for enhancement of compensation amount.
Since both these appeals arise out of the same judgment and award, they are taken up together for disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

4. It was the case of the petitioners that deceased Girish Maliye met with an accident on 30.10.2014 at 6.00 a.m. on Belagaum-Hindalaga road, due to rash and negligent driving of the tipper lorry bearing No.KA-22/B-4157 by its driver and as a result of the impact, the said Girish sustained grievous injuries and while undergoing treatment, he succumbed to the injuries.
5.
It was further case of the petitioners that deceased Girish was aged about 46 years at the time of accident.
He was businessman earning Rs.5,00,000/- p.m.
Petitioner No.1 is widow and petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are minor children of the deceased Girish and they were depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
With these reasons, petitioners had prayed to award compensation of Rs.8.00 crores.
6. Respondent No.1 was owner of the lorry bearing No.KA-22/B-4157 and respondent No.2 was insurer of the said lorry.
7. Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Tribunal and prosecuted the case.
8. Respondent No.2 before the Tribunal has denied all the averments stated in the petition.
It has also contended that accident had taken place due to negligence of the deceased and driver of the lorry had no valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident.
The owner and driver violated the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance.
Therefore, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
It has also contended that amount of compensation awarded is highly excessive.
With these reasons prayed to dismiss the petition.
9. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed relevant issues.
10. Claimants have examined P.Ws.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P12.

Respondent No.2 had examined R.Ws.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.R1 to R9.
11.

The Tribunal after appreciating the pleading, evidence and also arguments advanced by the learned counsels for both the side, partly allowed the petition and directed respondent No.1 to pay the compensation of Rs.38,05,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Claim against respondent No.2, was rejected.
12. We have heard the arguments of the learned counsel on both sides.

Mr.Khansab vs Smt.Ashalata on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84050292/
4 13.

The following points emerge for our determination:
1) Whether the Tribunal was justified in fastening liability on respondent No.1 to pay the compensation?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought in the appeal?
3) What order?
14.
Learned counsel for the claimants vehemently contended that Tribunal has not considered the income of the deceased properly.

The claimants had filed Exs.P9 to P11 i.e., income tax returns that discloses that gross income of the deceased was Rs.44,26,072/- for the financial year 2012-13, Rs.18,36,236/- for the financial year 2013-14 and Rs.28,98,158/- for the financial year 2014-15.
In addition to the said income from the business of Glow Cast, he was also partner in the firm, "Ventil Engineers" and getting share of profit from the said concern.

Ignoring all these facts,
the Tribunal has taken earnings of the deceased as Rs.25,000/- p.m., which is not proper.
The amount of compensation awarded under other heads are also meagre.
Therefore, prayed for enhancement of compensation.
He has also contended that driver of the lorry had valid driving licence and he had applied for renewal and thereafter, the licence to drive transport vehicle was given on 30.10.2014.

Therefore,
he had valid driving licence to drive the vehicle.

However, in the event, if it is held that driver had no valid and effective driving licence, at least in view of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in catena of judgments, the insurer shall be directed to pay the compensation and recover it from respondent No.1.
15.

Learned counsel for appellant in M.F.A.No. 103826/2016 respondent No.1 has contended that licence of the driver of the vehicle was renewed on 30.10.2014 at office hours whereas the accident had occurred at 6.00 a.m. on 30.10.2014.
On the basis of the evidence of R.W.1, the said driving licence was renewed at the office hours without producing any application or challan.
Unless the application or challan filed prior to renewal, the RTO would not renew the licence and hence, proviso to Section 15 of the M.V.Act provide for renewal from the date of application.
These are all the legal aspects and material documents have not been considered by the Tribunal.
The driver had valid and effective driving licence to drive transport vehicle which was renewed from 03.06.2013 to 02.06.2014.
In the interregnum period from 02.06.2013 to 29.04.2014, the driving licence was not renewed and driver of the vehicle had filed an application for renewal of the same.

In view of these circumstances, the Tribunal ought to have directed respondent No.2 to pay the compensation holding that driver of the lorry had valid and effective driving licence to drive the lorry.
He has further contended that amount of compensation awarded is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to reconsider the same and also direct respondent No.2 to pay the compensation.

Mr.Khansab vs Smt.Ashalata on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84050292/
5 16.

Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has contended that Tribunal has considered the fact that the driver of the lorry had no valid and effective driving licence and has rightly directed respondent No.1 to pay the compensation.
Since there was fundamental breach of the conditions of the policy of insurance, the insurer cannot be made liable to pay the compensation and recover it from owner of the vehicle.
With these reasons prayed to dismiss the petition.

17. The Tribunal appreciating the pleadings and evidence of the parties held that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry by its driver and in the said accident Girish had sustained injuries and died due to the said injuries.
This fact is not seriously disputed by either of the parties and it was not challenged.
Therefore, there is no need to reconsider the same.

18. In issue Nos.2 and 3, the Tribunal has re- appreciated the pleadings and evidence let in by the both the parties and held that income of the deceased was taken at Rs.25,000/- p.m., as supervisory charges.
His age was accepted as 46 years and proper multiplier was accepted as '13' and 30% of his income was added towards future prospects.
On that basis, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.33,80,000/- towards loss of dependency.
Looking to the assessment of income of the deceased, calculated by the Tribunal, needs to be reconsidered.
Claimants have produced Exs.P9 to P11, they are the income tax returns submitted for the period from 2012-13, 2013-14, 2014-15 and 2015-16.
Out of them, Exs.
P8 to P10 were filed during the lifetime of the deceased and Exs.P11 was filed by petitioner No.1.

In Exs.P8 to P10 income of the deceased was mentioned as Rs.44,26,072/-,
Rs.18,39,236/- and Rs.28,93,158/- respectively.

Ex.P8 was submitted on 18.09.2012, Ex.P9 was submitted on 21.05.2013 and Ex.P10 was submitted on 30.09.2014 and all these returns were submitted during the lifetime of the deceased Girish and they were submitted prior to the accident.
The said returns were also enclosed along with statement of accounts pertaining to the business by name "Glow Cast" said to be run in Machhe Industrial Area, Belagavi.
Looking to the said statement of accounts as well as income tax returns, it does not appear that for the sake of this case they were created as contended by Respondent.
The deceased might not be dreamt that he would die in an accident and to enable the legal heirs to claim compensation, the said records could be used.
Therefore, the said documents are reliable.

19. P.W.1 in her cross-examination has stated that her husband had studied Diploma in Automobile Course and he had been running the business for about 20 years prior to his death, by name "Glow Cast".
It was proprietary concern and it was registered.
More than 100 persons were working in the said company and after the death of her husband, the company has been transferred in her name and she had been conducting the business.
She has also stated that about 90 persons are still working in the company.

It was suggested to her by respondent No.2 that she has been earning profits as earned by her husband and she replied that, after she has been conducting business, she has suffered losses in the said company.
However, she has not explained what was the quantum of loss in the said business after the death of her husband.
20. She has examined P.W.2, who is Chartered Accountant of the said concern.
In the evidence of P.W.2, he has re-iterated about giving certificate of profit and loss account and also transferring of books of accounts of the said concern.

He did not explain in his cross-examination the loss suffered after the death of Girish and he has stated that on going through records, he could say the quantum Mr.Khansab vs Smt.Ashalata on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84050292/
6 of loss sustained by the said concern after the death of Girish.

entities.text: Mr.Khansab vs Smt.Ashalata on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2, it is clear that even after the death of Girish, the business concern established by him, has been running and P.W.1 has been earning income from the said business.
Though she has stated that she has suffered losses after the death of Girish, but she did not explain the quantum of loss.
No books of accounts have been produced by her.
Even the evidence of P.W.2 do not of much help to the petitioners, to show that due to death of Girish, PW-1 had suffered losses in the said business.
21. It is not in dispute that business was established and promoted by deceased Girish.
He was a technical expert and said to be holder of Diploma Course in Automobile.

It appears, due to his skill,
knowledge in the said field and exertion, he could establish the business and earn goodwill; because of which he could earn profit to an extent of Rs.44,26,072/- for the financial year 2012-13,
Rs.18,36,236/- for the financial year 2013-14 and Rs.28,98,158/- for the financial year 2014-15.
Due to entrepreneurship of deceased, he could commence and progress the business with in short time in a city like Belgaum, in Karnataka and earn so much of profit.
Petitioners failed to prove that after death of Girish, she had suffered loss or she was unable to continue the business.
In the absence of the same, it is to be believed that after the death of Girish his legal heir i.e., P.W.1 has been running the business and getting income from the said business.

22. The Tribunal on that basis held that he was entitled for supervisory charges of Rs.25,000/- p.m.;
and taken it as income of deceased and on that basis, it had held that family had been sustained loss of Rs.25,000/- p.m., which they had to pay towards supervisory charges.
The said calculation appears to be arbitrary.
Deceased was promoter of said business.

It appears due to his skill,
entrepreneurship and vision, he could start and develop said Industry.
Had he survived, he could develop the said Industry to much more Large Scale.
Due to his intelligence and skill in the field, he could establish a new concern and earn so much profit within a period of 20 years.
Due to his knowledge in the field, his expertise, skill, administration and management ability as well as salesmanship knowledge, he could enlarge his business and earn more profits.
All these skills cannot be equated by paying a meager sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m., as supervisory charges.
This could be payable to a normal employee of Group-'C' or 'D' in the said concern.
The standard of knowledge and goodwill he had earned has to be considered.
On the basis of these facts, it is taken as the family has lost atleast Rs.10,00,000/- p.a. for the supervisory charges as well as management of the said business.
23. Since deceased was aged about 46 years, as held in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, 30% of his income has to be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased left behind him his widow as well as two minor children.
Therefore, 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
The suitable multiplier applicable in this case is '13'.

Therefore, compensation for which the petitioners were entitled under (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 the head loss of dependency is Rs.8,66,667/- x 13 =
1,12,66,671/-.
24.

Petitioners are also entitled for compensation under conventional heads; as held in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram, each claimants/petitioners are entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Mr.Khansab vs Smt.Ashalata on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84050292/
7
Accordingly, Rs.1,20,000/- is awarded towards loss of spousal consortium and loss of parental consortium.
The petitioners are also entitled for Rs.15,000/- each under the head loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for total amount compensation of Rs.1,14,16,671/-, which is rounded off to Rs.1,14,17,000/- under the following heads:

Admittedly, the accident had taken place on 30.10.2014, Respondent No.2 examined R.W.1 i.e.,
RTO.
R.W.1 has stated that driving licence of driver of offending vehicle was renewed on 30.10.2014 during office hours on the said date.
Copy of the driving licence extract produced at Ex.R1.
It shows that licence to drive transport vehicle was given on 30.10.2014 and it was valid from 30.10.2014 to 29.10.2017.
It clearly shows that as on the date of the accident, driver of the said lorry had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the lorry.

The Tribunal has considered and appreciated the evidence properly and rightly held that driver of the lorry had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the lorry as on the date of the accident.

26. Respondent No.1 has filed MFA No. 103826/2016 and taken up lot of grounds in the appeal memo so also vehemently contended that the Tribunal has not at all directed respondent No.1 to produce the application given by the driver for renewal of licence; the Tribunal has not considered Article 15 of the M.V.Act to consider whether benefit of said rule was applicable to the driver of the lorry or not.
It is pertinent to note that respondent No.1 did not appear before the Tribunal and contested the matter.
He has not lead any evidence or produced any documents to show that driver of the lorry had given application and that application was not considered by the RTO.
Without raising any finger before the Tribunal, for the first time in this appeal has raised all these contentions, they are not tenable.
As per Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act, the person who had the knowledge about the fact, must prove the said contention.
Having failed to do so, now in this appeal, he cannot raise new grounds that Tribunal has not directed the RTO to produce the relevant records and they were not considered.
Even before this court also, the appellant has not produced any documents to show that driver of the lorry had given application well in time to renew licence.

Mr.Khansab vs Smt.Ashalata on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84050292/
8 27.
Learned counsel for respondent No.1 has contended that on 30.10.2014 the accident had taken place and the same day driving licence was renewed.
Therefore, it has to be considered that it was in force as on the date of the accident.
In support of his contention, he relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 3Union of India and Others vs. G.S.hatha Rice Mills and Another.

entities.text: 3Union of India and Others vs. G.S.hatha Rice Mills and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Principles of Law laid down in the said case are not applicable to the present case since facts are totally different.
The facts of the present case are very clear.
The accident had taken place on 30.10.2014 at 6.00 a.m.
But the RTO office commences its function at 10.00 a.m. to 5.30 p.m.
Therefore, it is also not the case of respondent No.1 that at 6.00 a.m., he could renew the said licence.
Under those circumstances, the above said judgment is not helpful to the contention of respondent No.1.
The Tribunal has rightly held that respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation.
Claimants are widow and minor children, who lost their earning member of the family.
It is not in dispute that package policy of insurance was taken on the said vehicle and it was in force as on the date of accident.
There is no fundamental breach of any condition of policy of insurance.

It is held by the Full Bench of this court in the case of 4New India Assurance Co.Ltd., Bijapur Vs Yallavva and Another, so also held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in catena of judgments, wherever there is no fundamental violation of conditions of policy insurance, the Insurer shall pay the compensation to the claimants and is at liberty to recover it from the owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: 4New India Assurance Co.Ltd., Bijapur Vs Yallavva and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same rule should also be made applicable to the facts of the present case.
Accordingly, respondent No.2 shall be directed to pay the compensation to the claimants and recover it from respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle.

29. In MFA No.103883/2016, the claimants have filed an application in I.A.No.1/2020 under Order 41 Rule 2020 (2) KCCR 1405 (FB) 27 of CPC for production of some of the documents, i.e., bank account statement and also VAT returns statement etc., for perusal of the Court.
No grounds made out as to why they were not produced before MACT.
Moreover, all these documents needs oral evidence to prove the same and it is also necessary for the claimants to explain about relevancy of the said documents for deciding the case.

Since this court has to consider income of the deceased,
therefore, these documents appears to be not relevant and do not help either of the parties to decide the matter fully and finally.
Accordingly, I.A.No.1/2020 is hereby rejected.

30. For the above said discussions, we answer the points accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER MFA No.103826/2016 filed by the owner of the vehicle is dismissed.
MFA No.103883/2016 filed by the claimants is allowed in part.
The impugned judgment and award is modified.

The claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,14,17,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till payment of enhanced amount, as against Rs.38,05,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

9
Respondent No.2-insurance company is directed to pay the said amount of compensation to the claimants and is at liberty to recover it from respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle.
The remaining portion of the impugned judgment are kept intact.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
All these skills cannot be equated by paying a meager sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m., as supervisory charges.
This could be payable to a normal employee of Group-'C' or 'D' in the said concern.
It clearly shows that as on the date of the accident, driver of the said lorry had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the lorry.
The Tribunal has considered and appreciated the evidence properly and rightly held that driver of the lorry had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the lorry as on the date of the accident.
As per Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act, the person who had the knowledge about the fact, must prove the said contention.
Having failed to do so, now in this appeal, he cannot raise new grounds that Tribunal has not directed the RTO to produce the relevant records and they were not considered.
Even before this court also, the appellant has not produced any documents to show that driver of the lorry had given application well in time to renew licence.
Therefore, it has to be considered that it was in force as on the date of the accident.
Principles of Law laid down in the said case are not applicable to the present case since facts are totally different.
The accident had taken place on 30.10.2014 at 6.00 a.m.
Therefore, it is also not the case of respondent No.1 that at 6.00 a.m., he could renew the said licence.
The Tribunal has rightly held that respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation.
(2021) 2 SCC 209 28.
Claimants are widow and minor children, who lost their earning member of the family.
It is not in dispute that package policy of insurance was taken on the said vehicle and it was in force as on the date of accident.
There is no fundamental breach of any condition of policy of insurance.
It is held by the Full Bench of this court in the case of 4New India Assurance Co.Ltd., Bijapur Vs Yallavva and Another, so also held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in catena of judgments, wherever there is no fundamental violation of conditions of policy insurance, the Insurer shall pay the compensation to the claimants and is at liberty to recover it from the owner of the vehicle.
